games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: This is Amal. ______ is presenting her booklet to the class.
rounds.explanation: Amal is one girl, so we use she. Unit 1 taught this pronoun.

rounds.prompt: The firefighters ______ helping on Warta Street.
rounds.explanation: Firefighters is more than one person, so the verb is are. This is the Unit 2 pattern.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence is a command?
choices: She is pointing at page four.
Amal will point at page four.
rounds.explanation: A command starts with the plain verb and tells somebody what to do, as in Unit 3.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence compares two things correctly?
choices: The metre is more long than the centimetre.
The metre is longest than the centimetre.
The metre is longer than the centimetre.
The metre long than the centimetre.
rounds.answer: The metre is longer than the centimetre.
rounds.explanation: Short describing words take -er plus than, which Unit 5 taught for measuring.

rounds.prompt: Which word tells you a position?
rounds.explanation: Under is a position word from Unit 6. Quickly tells how, butterfly names an insect and shouted is an action.

rounds.prompt: Which word is a describing word?
rounds.explanation: Bright describes the sky, as in Unit 4. Jump is an action, library names a place and quickly tells how.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What did Amal find at the very front of her English folder?
choices: Her welcome card from Unit 1, with her name written in careful blue letters.
Her hands felt cold, and she had to breathe slowly before she spoke.
It wants you to read every page aloud before you hand the booklet in.
rounds.answer: Her welcome card from Unit 1, with her name written in careful blue letters.
rounds.explanation: The first paragraph says the welcome card was at the front and the name was in careful blue letters.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence did Amal correct on her helpers page, and what did she change it to?
choices: She can already read shorter books by herself, so she is ready for something longer.
Page four, because it shows the sun and her long shadow.
She had written “The firefighters is working.” She changed it to “The firefighters are working.”
rounds.answer: She had written “The firefighters is working.” She changed it to “The firefighters are working.”
rounds.explanation: Paragraph four quotes both versions, so you must copy the corrected verb are.

rounds.prompt: Amal wrote that she wants to read a long chapter book next year. What does that tell you about her reading now?
choices: Adam said it was too short, so she added two facts about planting.
She can already read shorter books by herself, so she is ready for something longer.
It has four parts. In Part 3 you present your work for about two minutes.
rounds.answer: She can already read shorter books by herself, so she is ready for something longer.
rounds.explanation: This is an inference: the goal only makes sense if her reading has already grown this year.

rounds.prompt: From how many different units must the six booklet pages come?
choices: From at least four different units.
It has four parts. In Part 3 you present your work for about two minutes.
Nora likes the bug page and the butterfly wings, and Amal says she labelled the wings and the antennae.
rounds.answer: From at least four different units.
rounds.explanation: Part 1 of the brief says six pages from at least four different units.

rounds.prompt: The brief says your ears will find the missing full stops. What does it want you to do?
choices: From at least four different units.
Her welcome card from Unit 1, with her name written in careful blue letters.
It wants you to read every page aloud before you hand the booklet in.
rounds.answer: It wants you to read every page aloud before you hand the booklet in.
rounds.explanation: The last paragraph explains that reading aloud is how you hear a missing full stop.

rounds.prompt: How did Amal make her plant page better after she read it to Adam?
choices: She had written “The firefighters is working.” She changed it to “The firefighters are working.”
Adam said it was too short, so she added two facts about planting.
rounds.answer: Adam said it was too short, so she added two facts about planting.
rounds.explanation: Amal tells Leo exactly what feedback she was given and what she added because of it.

games.title: Memory Pairs
games.description: Reveal tiles and connect each word with its meaning.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 1.
pairs: use
To use something means to do a job with it.
kind
Kind means gentle and helpful towards other people.
tomorrow
Tomorrow means the day after today.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 2.
pairs: angry
Angry means you feel cross about something.
help
Help means to make something easier for someone by doing part of it.
adjectives
Adjectives are words that describe a person, a place or a thing.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 3.
pairs: main
Main means the most important part of something.
fix
Fix means to make something right after you find a mistake in it.
plan
A plan is a set of steps you make before you start something.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 4.
pairs: swallow
A swallow is a small bird with pointed wings that flies very fast.
butterfly
An insect with large, colourful wings that flies from flower to flower.
light
The brightness that lets us see things.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 5.
pairs: hand
The part at the end of your arm, with a thumb and fingers.
spell
To say or write the letters of a word in order.
event
Something special that happens, like a party or a game.

rounds.prompt: Match vocabulary set 6.
pairs: fact
A fact is something true that you can learn and tell other people.
tale
A tale is a story, often an old one that people retell.
whisper
To whisper means to speak very quietly.

rounds.prompt: There ______ three pictures beside the booklet.
